Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR CLIPS, PAPER 

( First Revision ) 


(Reaffirmed 2004) 
(Reaffirmed 2014) 


1. Scope — Specifies requirements for wire paper clips used to secure sheaves of paper. 

2. Material — Copper coated mild steel wire having minimum tensile strength of 685 N/mm* 
(70 kgf/mm*). 

3. Shape and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. 1.

4. Workmanship and Finish — The clTtML^;^)~lM;^is|jj^fomi^ and finished smoothly and evenly. 
They shall be free from seams, cracks, burrs, pits cmui}ISni^es of any kind when viewed under 10 X 
magnification. They shall be so formed that they show no tendency to tear or damage the paper when 
in use. Arms of the clips shall be parallel and close to each other to provide adequate grip and shall 
form flat loops except that the inner ioop shall have a slight upward bend at its tip for easy insertion. 
The ends shall be flat. The clips shall be cleaned and tumbled bright and shall be nickel plated. 

5. Tests 

5.1 Fatigue Strength — The clips shall adequately secure sheaves of paper thickness given below 
without undue setting to expanded form when used for 24 hours. 


Clip Size 

Small 

Large 


Thickness of 
Sheaf (mm) 


5.2 Corrosion Resistance Test — The clips shall be dipped in a solution of mineral spirit to remove any 
surface film or grease, and wiped dry. Five clips shall then be fastened to a strip of 75 mm x 50 mm of 
60 g/m® of white writing and printing paper [see IS : 1848-1981 'Specification for writing and printing

April 1989, BIS

papers {second revision)'}. Two such strips shall then be placed on the porcelain surface of the 
desiccator, the bottom of which shall be filled with 5 percent (m/m) aqueous solution of sodium 
chloride. The desiccator shall then be closed and allowed to stand for 24 hours. On removal from the 
desiccator, clips shall not show any sign of corrosion on point or the body of it when compared with 
the sample kept under identical conditions but without any aqueous solution in the desiccator. 

6. Packing —100 clips shall be packed in a carton of duplex board or pulp board of substance not 
less than 250 g/m^. Ten such cartons shall then be suitably packed in a bigger carton of cardboard of 
substance not less than 500 g/m^ Each bigger box shall be suitably closed by pasting tape around it to 
prevent tempering. Alternatively, it may be packed as agreed to between the purchaser and the 
supplier. 

7. Marking — Each carton or bigger box containing the clips shall be clearly and indelibly marked with 
the following information: 

a) Manufacturer's name, initials or registered trade-mark; 

b) Shape and size; 

c) Number of clips; 

d) Batch number; 

e) Year of supply; and 

f) Any other marking required by the purchaser. 

7.1 Standard Marking — Details available with the Bureau of Indian Standards. 

8. Sampling — Sampling scheme and acceptance criteria shall be as agreed to between the 
manufacturer and the purchaser. However, a recommended scheme for the same is given in 
Appendix A. 


APPENDIX A 

(Clause 8 ) 

SAMPLE CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY FOR CLIP PAPERS 


A-1. Lot 

A-1.1 In any consignment of the packets, paper clips of same dimensions produced under similar 
conditions out of the same raw-material shall be grouped together to constitute a lot. 

A*1.2 The number of packets to be selected from each lot shall depend on the size of the lot and shall 
be in accordance with Table 1. More or less an equal number of paper clips shall be chosen from the 
selected packets to constitute a sample size as given in Table 1. 

A-1.2.1 These paper clips shall be selected at random from the lot and for this purpose, procedure 
given in IS : 4905-1968 'Methods for random sampling' may be followed.
